The No. 4-ranked player in the 2027 recruiting class by 247Sports is the son of late NFL wide receiver Chris Henry

        Five-star forward Demarcus Henry committed to North Carolina on Friday, giving first-year coach Michael Malone his first major recruiting win on the high school trail. Henry, the No. 4 overall player and the top-ranked small forward in the 2027 recruiting cycle by 247Sports, is UNC's first commitment in the upcoming class.Henry is the son of late NFL wide receiver Chris Henry, who died in 2009. Henry's older brother, Chris Henry Jr., was a five-star wide receiver prospect in the 2026 class and is currently a freshman at Ohio State. The Compass Prep (Chandler, Arizona) product committed to North Carolina over Louisville, Arkansas and Kentucky. Henry took an official visit to North Carolina last weekend after previously visiting those three schools and UConn.247Sports Director of Scouting Adam Finkelstein says Henry's defensive upside is worth keeping an eye on.
Between his size, length, and movement skills, his defensive upside is extreme. He projects as being very switchable and already possesses impressive playmaking numbers with over 3 stocks per game in the EYBL (1.8 steals and 1.3 blocks). He's also an excellent wing rebounder who pulled down 9.2 (including 2.9 on the offensive end) in the EYBL and 8.4 in EYBL Scholastic play.Notably, Henry is the highest-ranked player in the 2027 recruiting class to announce his pledge. Beckham Black, CJ Rosser and Cayden Daughtry — the top-three ranked players in the upcoming recruiting cycle — remain uncommitted. This week, however, was busy on the high school front with several blue-chip players announcing their respective commitments. Henry was joined by Lewis Uvwo (Providence), Reese Alston (LSU) and Asa Montgomery (Duke) as players from the class who committed this week.

title: WNBA Finals Game 7 predictions: Will the Dream or Valkyries win their first title on Saturday? - CBS Sports
description: It's the first Game 7 in WNBA history on Saturday night in San Francisco ... so who will capture the crown?
body:
It's the first Game 7 in WNBA history on Saturday night in San Francisco ... so who will capture the crown?
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Oct 30, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:23 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It all comes down to Saturday in the 2026 WNBA Finals. It's Game 7 for the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream, and one franchise will win its first championship on Saturday night.The Dream forced this winner-take-all game -- the first Game 7 in WNBA history -- on Thursday. In a matinee at State Farm Arena, the Dream jumped out to a 25-point lead in the first half and held on for an 11-point win. Can Angel Reese and Atlanta finish the job on Saturday? Or will the Valkyries, Gabby Williams and a raucous home crowd propel Golden State to the title? We're making our picks below.WNBA Finals Game 7 picks
                    
    
                                            
                    
                                    Lindsay Gibbs
                            
            
                    
    
                                            
                    
                                    Jack Maloney
                            
            Valkyries vs. Dream
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Dream
                    
    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Valkyries
                    
    
    Gibbs: It feels fitting that this historic 30th WNBA season, that began with a hard-fought CBA that elevated player compensation into a new echelon, is ending in the league's first-ever Game 7.
But let's face it: This has not been a series of beautiful basketball. The Valkyries are shooting 34.5% from the field and 26.4% from 3 in the Finals, while the Dream are faring only marginally better, averaging 37.2% and 28.5%, respectively. However, it has been an incredibly compelling showcase of defense and mental fortitude, two aspects of the game that often get the short shrift. Both teams have had to pull themselves off the mat after punches that were potential knockouts; both teams have gained momentum just to have it halted; both teams have relied on their unity and self belief and confidence and grit to make it to this final do-or-die game.And now that we're here, it truly does feel like a toss-up. While the Dream's sensational first quarter on Thursday made the Game 7 possible, the way the Valkyries kept fighting in the game — winning the second half by nine points and whittling down a 25-point Dream lead to nine with just over a minute to play — set that Game 7 up to be a true prize fight. I keep thinking about what Veronica Burton said in the press conference after the Valkyries lost Game 6 in Atlanta by a score of 80-69."My body language is bad. But at the end of the day, we feel good. Yes, we lost. It was a bad game for us. We had a terrible first quarter. We cleaned it up. We found a way. We didn't quit," Burton said. "Games ... 2 and 3 were ugly. We quit. We looked bad, and we didn't quit on this one."The Valkyries were unable to match the Dream's sense of urgency in Game 6, but on Saturday, both teams will be facing elimination. Urgency should permeate every pass, every possession, every heart palpitation. Given the Valkyries are playing in front of their home crowd at Ballhalla, it is tempting to give them the edge.And yet, I'm still backing Atlanta. Earlier in this series, it was Angel Reese alone willing the Dream to wins in Game 2 and 3. But after a lackluster start to the series – and playoffs as a whole, truly – Rhyne Howard has found her stroke and averaged 19 points per game in the last four games of the Finals. And on Thursday, Allisha Gray – who has been playing the series with only eight healthy fingers after an injury in the semifinal series – came alive with 23 points. Essentially, there are three Dream players that I trust more than any Valkyries player to generate offense and make a basket when it matters the most.When we had to make our picks before the series, I picked Dream in 7 and wrote this:"In the spirit of Angel Reese and Joe Lacob, I am manifesting an epic seven-game series full of twists and turns. And, at the end, it will be a big defensive play by Reese that will seal the title for the Dream on the road in front of a raucous Ballhalla crowd on Halloween night."I've been wrong about so many things this postseason, but I'm still feeling good about that one. Dream in 7.Maloney: I picked the Valkyries in six before the series. That, obviously, can no longer happen, but I'm sticking with the Valkyries to win Game 7.The Dream have far more offensive upside, as we've seen at various points throughout this series, including the first quarter of Game 6, when they hit six 3-pointers and scored 32 points en route to a season-saving victory. But the Valkyries are one of the best defensive teams we've ever seen, and have spent much of the series dragging the Dream into the mud for a low-efficiency scrap. We saw that too in Game 6, when the Valkyries held the Dream to 48 points on 16-of-47 shooting (34%) with 15 turnovers.We've never had a Game 7 in the WNBA before, but we've seen the Finals go the distance plenty of times. And the winner-take-all contests to decide the title are often exactly the type of game the Valkyries want to play: slow-paced, low-scoring and extremely physical. In the last five winner-take-all games in the Finals, only one team -- the 2019 Washington Mystics -- has reached 80 points.
Last five winner-take-all games in WNBA Finals2024: Liberty 67, Lynx 622019: Mystics 89, Sun 782017: Lynx 70, Sparks 682016: Sparks 77, Lynx 762015: Lynx 69, Fever 52For whatever reason, be it the weird start time, fatigue or a sense of comfort after going up 3-2, the Valkyries didn't throw the first punch in Game 6, and the action got away from them."This is win or die. This is do or die. This is it," Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase said after Game 6. "You want to have that physicality. You want to have that fight. You want to lay it all out there. That's what the Finals is about is just an empty-the-tank mentality, and shoot, we didn't do that [Thursday]."Back in Ballhalla Boohalla, in front of a sold-out crowd on Halloween, the Valkyries will empty the tank in Game 7 and win the first championship in franchise history.

title: Anthony Colandrea returning to Nebraska in 2027: Huskers QB signs new deal - CBS Sports
description: Matt Rhule and the Huskers retained one of their top players before the start of a busy portal cycle
body:
Matt Rhule and the Huskers retained one of their top players before the start of a busy portal cycle

        Nebraska senior quarterback Anthony Colandrea has re-signed with the Huskers for the 2027 season, his agent confirmed to ESPN on Friday. Colandrea, who transferred last offseason from UNLV, has another year of eligibility due to the NCAA's "5-for-5" ruling and has been a much-needed, steady leader for the Huskers, throwing for 1,570 yards, 14 touchdowns and four interceptions to go along with 339 yards on the ground and four scores.This is the first known player contract extension in program history, continuing a trend in college football's new era of talent retention and contracts enabled by NIL and revenue sharing."In today's college football landscape, where the challenges and obstacles seem to multiply by the week, getting a process like this across the finish line as cleanly and seamlessly as we did is no small thing," Colandrea's agent Noah Reisenfeld wrote in a message to CBS Sports. "Pat Stewart, Logan Holgerson, and everyone in that building were nothing short of outstanding to work with through every step of it. Proud to have been a part of something this meaningful for Anthony and the program. Go Big Red."Earlier this month, Nebraska coach Matt Rhule said several SEC programs were already tampering with his quarterback ahead of this fall's transfer portal cycle, which officially begins Jan. 4 and closes nine days later.
"I don't think that's a good narrative for us to have out there that he doesn't have enough support," Rhule said. "I don't think that's good for our players. And not good because he's already got SEC schools calling him. I don't want Nebraska people to start saying that, because that's happened before here. We don't need that now here."Nebraska started the season 5-0 under Rhule before consecutive three-point losses to Indiana and Oregon this month torpedoed the team's shot at spearheading Big Ten championship efforts.The Huskers were on the verge of being ranked behind Colandrea's consistent play before those hiccups in the Big Ten games, during which Nebraska led in the fourth quarter.
"Like I said, I think we're two plays away from being in the big, big conversation," Rhule said entering last week's open date ahead of Saturday's return to the field vs. Washington. But we're not out yet, so we're going to just try to get better this week."Colandrea's impact for Huskers in 2027Colandrea is the second standout this season to re-sign with his current program, joining Oregon State's Jesse Legree, one of the nation's leading wide receivers. Colandrea brought stability to Nebraska's offense after the Huskers watched former five-star Dylan Raiola leave after the 2026 campaign and transfer to Oregon.Entering Week 9, Colandrea and the Huskers rank second in the Big Ten in scoring offense (35.5 points per game), fifth in total offense and third in explosive plays. Colandrea has been an ideal fit in Dana Holgorsen's scheme given his dual-threat ability and wrinkle in a run game that is the most potent of Rhule's tenure at 194.3 yards on the ground per game.
Colandrea said before the season he felt Nebraska's offensive line was the best he had ever played with and trusted that would be one of the strengths of the team. The Huskers allotted a chunk of this season's football share to their offensive front, including the acquisition of former South Carolina tackle "Big" Tree Babalade in the portal.The return of QB1 in 2027 for Rhule is the first piece of the puzzle for a team with College Football Playoff expectations, given the skill talent coming back and the likelihood of the 24-team expanded postseason being beneficial in the Big Ten.

The German manager is facing pressure after a disappointing start of the 2026-2027 season

        Saturday's match between Udinese and AS Roma will likely decide the future of Bianconeri head coach Kosta Runjaic. The German manager, who made a surprise move to Udinese in the summer of 2024, enjoyed a positive start to his spell at the club. He guided the team to 12th place in his first season and then 10th in the following campaign, while implementing an attractive style of football and helping several key players fulfill their potential. Among them were Nicolo Zaniolo, defender Oumar Solet, English striker Keinan Davis and Arthur Atta, who joined Fiorentina this summer.However, things became difficult in the first part of the 2026-27 season, and Saturday's match against AS Roma could be a crucial test for his future at the club. Udinese lost six games in a row before drawing 0-0 away to Parma on Wednesday. Despite a solid start to the season, with a convincing home draw against Como on the opening day followed by an away win at Monza, Udinese are now 17th in the standings, with only nine goals scored and 18 conceded in nine matches. That is why the game, played on Halloween, could be the last call for his future at the club, even though the ownership has backed him and confirmed he will stay in the job at least until the November international break. How to watch Udinese vs. RomaDate: Saturday, Oct. 31 | Time: 1 p.m. ETLocation: Bluenergy Stadium -- Udine, ItalyTV: CBSOdds: Udinese +448; Draw +337; AS Roma -198Before Udinese's away draw against Parma, sporting director Gianluca Nani called for a reaction from the team after a challenging moment. "We are coming off six consecutive defeats, but we firmly believe that this team is not who we really are. We are the same side that put in some impressive performances, against Como, for example, and also against Lazio. This is not an easy period, and it is our responsibility to turn things around and get back on the path we set out on two years ago," he told DAZN.He added, "Performances like the one against Lecce are unacceptable, and the players know that. We want to see greater focus on individual moments in the game. In the other matches, the performances have always been there. Take the game in Turin, for example: we should have won that one. The team must give everything, because when you do that, the results will follow. We are going through a difficult spell, but we must not be afraid. Instead, we need to find the motivation to get through it. It is up to us to turn things around."
Keinan Davis on Morning FootyUdinese striker Keinan Davis spoke to CBS Sports Golazo's Morning Footy ahead of the clash with AS Roma, discussing the differences between playing in Serie A and English football: "It's good to be honest. It's to be fair, when people ask me it's kind of like Stevenage where it's just like its own town and it's just kind of slow, you know. So it was quite easy in that sense to adapt. It's not like fast-paced or anything. And then just the people, they just love football, you know. Italians, they just love their football, and it's kind of where they wear their heart on their sleeve, and they're so passionate, you know. So obviously we're passionate about football as well, so it just goes hand in hand. And then on that side of things, it just takes care of itself, you know, you spend a lot of time in the training ground. You're back at home, you might go to a restaurant or something, and it's just all love really."  "Compared to England, it's much slower, I'd say. And more it's more structured and tactical. You get, like less 1v1 kind of actions. In the Premier League or in the Championship, you get a lot of, like, wing play. Here they play a lot of five at the back. So it's usually wing-backs and a lot of crosses and stuff like that. Up against three defenders when you're a lone striker, you obviously got so many battles you got to come across in the game. And England is very different; you get like a lot of 1v1 actions or a lot of just like where you'd have to use your physicality more. Over here it's kind of just using your mind more, being in the right position at the right time, I'd say."He also underlined the differences in the life he's having in Italy. "To be honest, I prefer the food in England than to Italy, which is crazy. I said this before when I got here, but yeah. I'm just a very basic eater, you know? And I'm very picky as well so I don't like too much sauce or too much stuff like that. So the food I get in England is just it suits me."How de Roon is adapting in RomeAS Roma midfielder Marten de Roon also joined the Morning Footy crew to discuss his impact at the club after his surprise summer move from Atalanta. De Roon, who previously played under Roma coach Gian Piero Gasperini at Atalanta, seemed happy to be working with him again: "I'm happy to re-find him and it was like he's never gone away. Still the same ideas, some developments, but in the end, yeah, his playing style, the way he wants to do things, I still memorize it. So, it was quite easy to adapt to his playing style. The most important thing for me was to get back in condition because he's a coach who asks a lot from the players in the physical way. So, I needed some time to get back in condition. But now, yeah, I feel good. It's been amazing, the first two months, and yeah, really, really happy to be back with him as my coach." 
Later, he added: "I think the strength so far this season is that there's a real feeling for the team, the group. You see also in difficult moments like last week, but also against Napoli. We were behind and then we found the way to draw, to score goals. And he made a lot of changes, guys who came in. So it looks like the group is quite big, that we can play with different players at the same level. We don't lose quality by changing players. And I think that's the most important thing, that even when somebody is feeling less for a day that there's someone else who can replace him and give the same amount of quality. And I think if we can continue this and even find some players back, and I think we have about 19, 20 players who can all play, and I think that, yeah, that makes the level even better for the team."

title: Nick Saban advises Texas, Steve Sarkisian to use 'the bench' to motivate Arch Manning - CBS Sports
description: Saban had no problem benching high-profile players in big spots during his legendary coaching career
body:
Saban had no problem benching high-profile players in big spots during his legendary coaching career
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 30, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:26 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Arch Manning's inconsistency has plagued the Texas offense this season, and a recent threat from Steve Sarkisian potentially prompted the former five-star quarterback to play with more poise last time out, according to Nick Saban.Saban was no stranger to benching players in his time at Alabama. He famously sat Jalen Hurts in favor of Tua Tagovailoa at halftime of the Tide's 2018 national title game against Georgia, prompting a memorable comeback win. "I always say the bench is a pretty good motivator, especially if the guy's a great competitor, which I think Arch is," Saban said Friday on ESPN. "The threat that he might not be entitled to the job may be something that motivates him and keeps him motivated through the rest of the season. He's going to have to play well for them to be able (to win out)."Backup KJ Lacey has played sparingly this season despite a recent reported uptick in first-team reps during practice, and hasn't faced the complexity of live SEC rounds like Tagovailoa.In both of the Longhorns' losses this season, Manning made critical fourth-quarter mistakes that swung the game's momentum, and he did it against Ole Miss too with the game tied, but Texas escaped.
"Sark made it very clear when he had a meeting with Arch and said to him, 'Look, we can't win with this guy,'" Saban said. "It's always a tough decision for a coach to make a change like that when you have a high-profile player who's very capable and has shown at times he's very capable. But at the same time, I think if Arch doesn't continue to play with consistency, Sark's going to keep it in the bag."What Texas faces nextAfter Saturday's game against Mississippi State, the No. 11 ranked Longhorns (5-2) embark on a season-defining November stretch that includes trips to ranked Missouri and LSU before Arkansas and Texas A&M round out the campaign.Texas is currently slotted as an at-large selection in our updated College Football Playoff projections entering the weekend and ahead of Tuesday night's first CFP top 25 reveal from the selection committee.
Winning out all but guarantees a spot in the CFP and could get Texas to another SEC Championship appearance. Going 4-1 over their final five games means the Longhorns likely find themselves in a logjam of nine-win SEC teams. Then it comes down to overall resume and whatever the selection committee chooses to deem important during the final process.

title: MLS reveals 2027 sprint season schedule ahead of shift to European calendar - CBS Sports
description: Each club will play 14 regular-season games from February to May before a 16-team single-elimination playoff crow
body:
Each club will play 14 regular-season games from February to May before a 16-team single-elimination playoff crowns a champion
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 30, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:27 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        While the MLS regular season has yet to come to a close, the details of the sprint season have now been released. The sprint season is a critical bridge to the league moving to a European calendar, as the 2027 season will take place under a condensed schedule in order to prepare for that. Each team will play 14 regular season matches, with one home and one away. The regular season will run from February 19, with Inter Miami and FC Cincinnati kicking things off, until Decision Day on May 8t, when there's a Hudson River Derby between New York City FC and New York Red Bulls to close out the season. With NYCFC set to open a new stadium in Queens, this should also be the final MLS game played at Yankee Stadium, which NYCFC have called home since joining the league in 2015. Truly the end of an era that went on for far too long.Ahead of the shift, MLS wants to ensure that each week has a marquee matchup to highlight the best of what the league has to offer. There will also be another season of the Walmart Saturday Showdown and of Sunday Night Soccer, so that the biggest games of the week get their due credit. With stars from abroad such as Antoine Griezmann, Lionel Messi, Thomas Muller, and Evander pitting against young stars such as Cavan Sullivan, Julian Hall, Adri Mehmeti, and Peyton Miller, there's plenty to showcase as MLS prepares for a new era.
A playoff shiftThe top eight teams in each conference will qualify for the playoffs, with each round being played in a single-elimination format. That schedule is yet to be announced, but it will see a shift from the current format, where the eighth- and ninth-placed teams play a single-elimination wild card match prior to the first round being a best-of-three series. That playoff format has seen criticism due to being too long, so the sprint season does offer an opportunity to take a look at other formats ahead of a return to a standard schedule in the fall. Still, using playoffs will ensure that all five Concacaf Champions Cup spots are accounted for before the teams also return to full participation in the Lamar Hunt U.S. Open CupWhy change the schedule?This split will help get MLS onto the same transfer market as the rest of the world. MLS doing their primary transfer window in the winter has long been an issue due to teams not being able to send players to America. It also could mean that MLS sides won't be pressured to sell their best players midseason, either with the summer transfer window being an enticing time for teams to wade in and get new players during their own preseason. The change will bring geographic challenges such as dealing with harsh winters, but those are no different from the thunderstorm and extreme heat risks that the league already faces during the summer months in such varied climates. With the shift also including teams stopping play for international breaks, it will also end the need to play without your best players available, which increases the quality in the league.
2027 MLS Sprint Season by the numbersAll teams will play 14 regular-season games.Each team will play its 14 conference opponents one time.All teams will play seven home games and seven away games in the regular season.The top eight teams from the Eastern Conference and the top eight teams from the Western Conference will qualify for the Audi MLS Cup Playoffs.One team will be crowned MLS Cup champions.Five Concacaf Champions Cup berths will be determined by the 2027 MLS Sprint Season results.In total, 18 teams will qualify for the Leagues Cup, nine from each conference.Following the conclusion of this sprint season, the 2027-28 MLS Season will kick off in July of 2027. It will then conclude with the MLS Cup playoffs, which will run until May of 2028, similarly to when most European leagues wrap up.

title: CeeDee Lamb says Cowboys have a Cardinals boogeyman: 'They've punched us in the mouth every single time' - CBS Sports
description: Dallas five-time Pro Bowl wide receiver CeeDee Lamb has never beaten Arizona, and they have won eight of the last
body:
Dallas five-time Pro Bowl wide receiver CeeDee Lamb has never beaten Arizona, and they have won eight of the last nine matchups
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 30, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:45 pm ET

        FRISCO, Texas — The Dallas Cowboys (3-4) have an Arizona Cardinals (2-5) problem they're looking to halt in Week 8. Arizona has won four consecutive games against Dallas as part of a larger span of success that includes wins in eight of the last matchups dating back to 2008. Cowboys five-time Pro Bowl wide receiver CeeDee Lamb, who is in his seventh NFL season in 2026, has never beaten Arizona, losing all four matchups since he was drafted by Dallas in 2020. Why has Dallas struggled so much against the Cardinals? CBS Sports asked Lamb about that and if he has a heightened focus entering the matchup. Lamb's answer? The Cardinals have seemingly wanted it more. "I've never beaten the Cardinals since I've been in the league. So that's fair to say," Lamb said after practice on Thursday. "I wouldn't say [we have a] heightened focus, but it's definitely a note to take. It's just crazy. We've been very relaxed, and they've punched us in the mouth every single time. They've always had more energy. "Just coming into the game, they're more excited regardless of if it was at 12 o'clock [1 Eastern], Monday night, Sunday night. We played them in primetime; they beat us there. Just coming in and treating them as if they are a Super Bowl-contending team, which they may be. Hats off to them in their prep. We just have to go match them, if not overpower that."   
Dallas head coach Brian Schottenheimer disagreed with his top target's assessment, instead pointing to "the ball." The Cowboys have a -11 turnover margin (15 turnovers to four) across the nine matchups since 2008. In Dallas' "Monday Night Football" home loss in Week 9 last season, the Cowboys committed three turnovers and didn't generate a takeaway. Quarterback Dak Prescott had an interception, and both running back Javonte Williams and tight end Jake Ferguson lost fumbles. That put the Cowboys in a 17-point hole minutes into the second half.Arizona's win against Dallas in 2025 was the only victory in 12 starts for Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett in 2025.  Schottenheimer has a point. Across all three of the Cowboys' wins this season, they have committed zero turnovers. All four of Dallas' losses in 2026 involve at least one turnover. "I'll disagree with CeeDee a little bit," said Schottenheimer on Friday. "I know why: minus-11 turnover differential in those games. Last year, we were minus-three. So the ball is what this game is going to come down to. I don't think it has to do with energy." 
Cowboys vs. Cardinals, Last 18 yearsResultWeek 9, 2025 (MNF)Cardinals 27, Cowboys 17Week 3, 2023Cardinals 28, Cowboys 16Week 17, 2021Cardinals 25, Cowboys 22Week 6, 2020 (MNF)Cardinals 38, Cowboys 10Week 3, 2017 (MNF)Cowboys 28, Cardinals 17Week 9, 2014Cardinals 28, Cowboys 17Week 13, 2011Cardinals 19, Cowboys 13Week 16, 2010Cardinals 27, Cowboys 26Week 6, 2008Cardinals 30, Cowboys 24Dallas should be able to stop the slide on Sunday as seven-point home favorites, according to DraftKings Sportsbook. The Cardinals enter Week 8 as the NFL's worst scoring defense, allowing 29.7 points per game. Offensively, Arizona enters Week 8 as the league's worst red zone offense, scoring touchdowns on just 42.9% of its red zone drives. Dallas enters Week 8 as the NFL's No. 5 scoring offense (27.0 points per game), with new cornerback Joey Porter Jr. helping calm things down for Dallas' defense. There's only one way for the Cowboys to bury their Cardinals boogeyman narrative: just win. "We got to win," said Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott after practice on Thursday. "They've had our number these last couple of years. Credit to their defense, credit to the way that those guys come in and play and execute. It's a new year. We just have to make sure we go out and take care of business."

        If last season's visit to Anfield taught Arsenal anything, it was the need for a killer in the final third to break the game open. Fail to do so and they are vulnerable to the sort of magic that bamboozled them in August of last year, even if the man who scored that brilliant free-kick winner, Dominik Szoboszlai, is a doubt for Liverpool on Sunday.And if this game is indeed one that will be decided by what Mikel Arteta terms the "moments players," then it could scarcely have come at a worse time for the Arsenal manager. Bukayo Saka -- the Gunners' top shot taker, goal scorer and expected goals compiler -- has more than a month left on the sidelines with the thigh injury he suffered in Munich. Noni Madueke could miss the trip with an ankle injury. Christos Tzolis has returned to training but has not played for his new club in more than a month. Max Dowman, the precocious youngster whom Arteta has already entrusted with turning the tide on Merseyside, will serve the first of a three-game ban for his controversial red card.It speaks to the depth at Arteta's disposal that, even if none of the aforementioned quartet play, there will still be game changers in the side. Even so, this does feel like an occasion where a first-choice center forward in top form would be handy. Kai Havertz is not that. Twelve games in and this has been perhaps the weirdest season of all since this esoteric forward landed on English soil in 2020. At his best, he has blown his former club Chelsea away. His worst, meanwhile, includes a wasteful performance in the EFL Cup defeat at Fleetwood and a baffling new tendency to slip offside. 
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            The obvious answer when a player slides from peak to trough in a matter of weeks is to consult his injury record. Havertz did return from the last international break early after straining a muscle and went straight back into the side, playing an hour against Leeds and featuring in every other game since. In those six games he has no goals and one assist. In most of the minutes he has played, he has struggled to link the Arsenal attack together the way he usually does, let alone to threaten the opposition goal. That is not, however, a hangover from his injury travails.
"There's nothing to do with that," said Arteta. "It's true that in terms of the numbers, we have dropped those numbers but he certainly had the chances as well to play."That was the case against Fleetwood, seven shots for the German adding up to 0.72 expected goals. That sounds perfectly adequate on first pass, and there are certainly others in the Arsenal side who ought to have asked more of a League Two defense. And yet when chasing a game for 70 minutes, is it fair to ask for more than three-quarters of an xG from the senior attacker of the English champions, a man who has scored in two Champions League finals?Wanting a bit more has been a familiar experience for both Chelsea and Arsenal during his time with them. For the Gunners, it has been over two and a half years since they discovered just how good Havertz could be for them. The shift to center forward in a 3-1 win over Sunday's opponents, Liverpool, was the start of a brilliant year leading the line. Across 37 Premier League games, the Germany international delivered 18 goals and nine assists, not Erling Haaland numbers but exceptional output for the center forward in Arteta's everyone-eats offense.
Even since that brilliant run, there have been flashes. For an hour in May's Champions League final, Havertz was as threatening an attacker as anyone in PSG colors. A few weeks earlier he had been excellent in defeat to Manchester City, not the first time he had bossed Arsenal's title rival. If Chelsea have the misfortune of running into their former star, they're probably going to get him in the mood to do some damage. Of all the attackers available to Arteta this week, Havertz is the nearest he has to a big-game hunter.  Indeed, if you want to make the case against Arsenal "just signing a striker" in January (you shouldn't), a key component of your argument ought to be how few players suit this manager as well as a fully fit Havertz. It is just that, well, a fully fit Havertz has been an elusive creature.  And yet if Arteta will not use injuries as justification for the current wobble, perhaps we shouldn't. And wobble this is. Through eight league games, Havertz is averaging fewer shots, goals and non-penalty xG than in any other season in his Arsenal career on a per-90 basis. The same is true when you adjust for the fact that the 27-year-old is touching the ball a bit less on average this season than last.  There is one notable stat where Havertz's numbers have skyrocketed, though, and that is in offsides. In every Premier League season before this one, he was caught out behind the opposition defense on less than one occasion per 90 minutes. In most of them, he averaged around one offside per two full games played. This year, however, no one in the league matches Havertz's 10 offsides already, and the gap is not particularly close. Joint-second on seven are his teammate Bukayo Saka and Dominic Calvert-Lewin of Leeds.Passes made by Arsenal this season that resulted in their players being caught offside 
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            Now, the sample size of minutes is still small and open to distortion. It might be that one explanation for Havertz's skyrocketing offsides is that he has played Aston Villa and their occasionally effective, invariably cavalier high line. Equally, not all of those 10 offsides are about what the defense did well or about a run that came at just the wrong moment from the center forward. Watch Havertz move a good moment too soon to collect a pass off his friend and captain Martin Odegaard before bending well wide from a promising shooting position against Villa, and you see what looks like a forward who is simply off color, nothing more and nothing less, really. Sometimes the easiest explanation is the correct one. Havertz is just a bit out of sync with both his game and that of his teammates, as his manager acknowledged on Friday."That kind of form and that kind of efficiency with the front players, it's very common," said Arteta. "Full trust on him and what he's doing."
The natural response, then, for Arteta would be to pick the next cab off the rank, as he did in the win over Everton where Viktor Gyokeres started. That was the Swede's best game of the season, but he still did not register a shot. Gyokeres scored against Fleetwood but took only two other shots. Per 90, he averages 0.92 shots, 16th on Arsenal, with both left backs ahead of him. The evidence of his past entanglements with elite opposition suggests that Gyokeres is not the player to turn to at Anfield.Instead, it will be Havertz, in need of something of a jump-start to his season. While he retains the "full trust" of a manager who has never faltered in his support, there might be time enough to sniff out his best form. Viewing information -- Liverpool vs. ArsenalDate: Sunday, Nov. 1 | Time: 11:30 a.m. ETLocation: Anfield, Liverpool, United KingdomTV: USA | Live stream: fuboTVOdds: Liverpool +188; Draw +230; Arsenal +138

A 13-6 win in overtime against a listless Michigan team didn't assuage those concerns, and now they welcome a Minnesota team that has proven to be a thorny opponent. The Gophers come in at 5-2 fresh off a 13-10 win over Iowa to hoist the Floyd of Rosedale trophy, as PJ Fleck is 2-for-2 in rivalry games this season. Minnesota will need to step up their level in the next two games against top-10 foes in Indiana and UCLA, but if the Hoosiers get caught looking ahead to a trip to USC, they can quickly find themselves in a dogfight with the Gophers despite being 20.5-point favorites. Will the Hoosiers' offense come to life back at home and re-establish themselves as one of the nation's elite? Can Minnesota pull off another stunner by dragging Indiana into the mud? We'll find out on Saturday afternoon in what could be another thrilling, tense Big Ten battle. 
  Minnesota vs. Indiana: Need to know  Hoosiers need more from Hoover: Indiana's still a top 5 team, but this is clearly not a squad at the same level as last year. That's largely due to an offense stuck in the mud, with a quarterback who has not clicked with the scheme despite two highly talented receivers on the outside. Josh Hoover has been dreadful the last few weeks, and when the Hoosiers have won, it's been in spite of their quarterback's play. That might not need to change to win this week specifically, but the Hoosiers are desperate to establish some form of offensive rhythm in the back half of the season before the College Football Playoff. The Gophers present challenges, but this is the caliber of team Indiana should be able to handle with ease. They've not proven to have that gear so far this season, and it's incumbent on Hoover to be both more dynamic and more efficient throwing the football for them to find that next level. 
DE-FENSE [clapclapclap]: The defenses for both teams are their point of strength, and both teams will be looking to their defensive playmakers to help them out. The Hoosiers and Gophers put forward defensive masterclasses in low-scoring wins a week ago, but Minnesota is the team with the greater questions on that side of the ball. There have been games where Minnesota looks fantastic defensively (like last week against Iowa), but they have struggled against teams that can stretch the field and have high-level athletes on the outside. Indiana has that in Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh, but the question is whether Josh Hoover can get them the ball on time and on target regularly enough to take advantage of their mismatches. Indiana has no such questions, and they'll start by trying to take away Minnesota's ground game and dare Drake Lindsey to beat them through the air. 
Can Drake Lindsey protect the football? There's a world where the Gophers hang around in this one and are a live dog on the road to pull a stunning upset. However, that only happens if Lindsey protects the football, something he's not excelled at this season. Lindsey leads the Big Ten with six interceptions and has thrown at least one in each of Minnesota's last five games. The Gophers have to maximize every possession to have a chance against Indiana, and given the Hoosiers have an elite defense, there won't be any room for error on Lindsey's part. He came into the season with NFL Draft buzz because of his physical tools, but he's got to manage risk better in the second half of the season to boost that stock. Saturday will be his biggest test yet on the road. Where to watch Minnesota vs. Indiana live  Date: Saturday, Oct. 31 | Time: 3:30 p.m. ET  Location: Memorial Stadium -- Bloomington, Indiana
TV: CBS | Live stream: CBSSports.com, CBS Sports App  Streaming on Paramount+ Premium  Minnesota vs. Indiana prediction, picks  If it ain't broke, don't fix it. The Hoosiers are quite simply an under machine right now. It's not just that they have an elite defense and a sputtering offense, but it's the way Curt Cignetti is managing games. The lack of trust in Hoover is never more apparent than when he trots the punt unit out on a fourth-and-short at midfield without hesitation. Even if Indiana dominates, it's hard to see them piling up points on a good Minnesota defense, and there's a real world where the Gophers keep this close throughout. title: Why Yaxel Lendeborg could be the key to saving what's left of the Warriors' Stephen Curry era - CBS Sports
description: After Yaxel Lendeborg decided to start a war of words with Luka Dončić both during and after his first NBA game last week --more or less
body:
After Yaxel Lendeborg decided to start a war of words with Luka Dončić both during and after his first NBA game last week --more or less calling one of the best players in the world a crybaby for whom he "lost all respect" -- both Stephen Curry and Steve Kerr remarked that they were fine with the don't-give-a-damn brashness of the Warriors' rookie. Curry and Kerr even said that they liked it, but with the caveat that he would, of course, have to "back it up."How's that going so far? Well, put it this way: If Lendeborg keeps playing like this, the only other thing he's going to have to back up is a Brinks truck to collect his next contract. Through his first five games, the No. 11 overall pick is averaging 22.6 points, 9.6 rebounds and four assists. Those are not just All-Star numbers. Those are historic numbers. Let's break them down.Yaxel joining elite companyLet's start with the basics: Lendeborg is the first Warriors rookie since Stephen Curry to score at least 25 points in three straight games. That's more of a footnote considering Golden State's many draft whiffs over the last 15 years, but still, this is no easy feat over any three-game rookie stint, let alone inside the first two weeks of your career. 
OK, now let's get to the bigger stuff. Lendeborg is the first rookie in nearly 70 years to record at least 100 points, 45 rebounds and 20 assists through his first five games. His 113 total points are the third-most this century through the first five games of a career, trailing only Kevin Durant and Paolo Banchero. Toss in his 46 rebounds and he's the first player to reach those five-game scoring/rebounding marks since Shaquille O'Neal in 1992. Add in his 20 assists, and only one other player NBA history -- a pretty good one, it turns out -- is in his company. 
Putting up these kinds of numbers can only happen, one, if you've got the game, but two, and in the context of the Warriors this may be the even more important part, if you're given the opportunity to do so. Which brings us to ...Yaxel has Steve Kerr's trustThis is no small feat. Maybe it's because he's an old rookie. He's 23. Spent six years in college. Started at a junior college. Grinded through every level and has the maturiity in both game and mind to show for it. This is important, because it would be easy to classify Lendeborg as immature for all his spouting off, but much like Draymond, listen to what he's actually saying rather than how or to whom he's saying it. Before you go off in judgment of a man with an opinion, understand that he's earned his maturity in ways that, frankly, a guy like Dončić hasn't. 
Luka was a prodigy from Day 1, and was treated as such. That isn't a shot at Luka. It's just the reality. Yaxel has worked real jobs in the real world. He didn't even play sports when he first got to high school. He was trying to make money in the same warehouse in which his mom worked. 
Don't confuse Yaxel having strong opinions with being a know-it-all. The smartest players, and people, seek wisdom, and Yaxel has talked repeatedly about sponging off Curry and Green. After putting up 31 points, 12 rebounds and six assists against Denver, he used his postgame interview with ESPN's studio show to solicit advice from Vince Carter, Carmelo Anthony and Tracy McGrady. I take great pride in my cynicism, and normally this kind of platform pandering would trigger all the eye-rolling alarms, but Lendeborg appears to be so authentic that you honestly believe he's asking the greats for tips on national television because he actually wants the tips. 
When Yaxel talked about the league being full of floppers, the part that didn't get circulated was him saying he is going to learn all the tricks to take "as many free throws as possible." Even when he's criticizing something, he's clocking it, too. This is a clearly an observant and, contrary to the trash-talking perceptions, humble guy who has spoken about wanting to leave Kerr with the impression of "someone who's willing to learn" and hold himself to a standard worthy of a championship coach's trust. For instance, you may think putting up 26 points and nine boards in your fifth career game, as Lendeborg did in a win over the Wolves on Wednesday, is a great showing, but Lendeborg described his performance as "hella soft" while lamenting a "timid" approach that led to him committing seven turnovers. Kerr has noted that Lendeborg needs to improve his weak-side defensive focus, that he can run the floor harder, and that he tried to "force a lot of plays" against Minnesota (Kerr has talked about sometimes it being as simple as taking one more dribble before taking to the air on a drive), which was a point he made after Lendeborg went for 26 points, nine rebounds and five assists against Phoenix. 
This is a fine line for a 6-foot-9, 250-pound "strong as an ox" guy who butters a lot of bucket-getting bread with power drives. Draymond is telling Yaxel to go through defenders' chests, while Kerr is telling him to him to slow down, see the floor and make sound decisions without compromising aggression. There's nuance and interpretation in both those messages, and surely this is the stuff that Kerr, Green, Curry and all the other Golden State vets are going to be talking with Yaxel about all year. Mistakes are sometimes the most important ingredient in a developmental stew. That's where the learning comes from, and Yaxel is certainly going to travel a steep curve on his way to finding his strength-skill sweet spot, particarly within the context of a team that needs him to make things happen. Somewhere Jonathan Kuminga is surely wondering why he was never afforded the luxury of playing through his mistakes, while Lendeborg is crashing into defenders and committing 18 turnovers over his last four games and still leading the team in minutes. 
To that, allow me to summon my inner-Yaxel and not beat around the bush with this one: He's worlds better than Kuminga (who never embraced or more importantly improved upon any part of the game other than scoring) ever was for the Warriors. And besides that, Kuminga wasn't, and isn't, the non-interruptive scorer that Lendeborg has already showed himself to be anyway, to say nothing of all the other basketball boxes he checks. ✅Elite positional size✅Floor spacer✅Transition freight train✅One-on-one creator✅Pick-and-roll initiator✅Grab-and-go pace pusher✅Half-court ball handler✅Natural facilitator✅Big-boy rebounder✅Physical, athletic defenderYou can see the whole Yaxel package in this reel below. The bully, through-the-chest drives and a deceleration finish that speaks to the composed attacks Kerr wants to see more of. The spot-up shooting (8 of 12 from 3 so far on these shots, per Synergy). The chase-down block on one end into a floor-running finish on the other. The athletic cuts. The savvy pick-and-roll feel (watch him smoothly split the defenders at the 1:25 mark). Pay close attention to the way Yaxel spins into the lane for a finish on Nikola Jokić at the 16-second mark, and then, later, how he makes the same move but this time the defense collapses and he recognizes it immediately and zips a pass to the corner for a Brandin Podziemski 3. 
Kerr has called Lendeborg "100%" the most pro-ready rookie that he's ever coached, noting that he knew Lendeborg had the shoot-pass-dribble skill package to be effective right away, but that he also "has a better feel for the game than I realized." That's why Kerr trusts him to not just be on the floor more than any other player so far, but to actually pilot an offense that is registering a top-five rating during his minutes, per Cleaning the Glass. 
"Basically, at all the critical moments of the game, we just put the ball in his hands," Kerr said after that Denver game. "For a rookie to be that advanced already, it's extremely rare."Does Yaxel change Warriors' short-term plan?Long term, Lendeborg looks like the next-era star that Joe Lacob has been desperate to land since the start of the decade, which he seemingly thought was the beginning of Curry's end. Lacob was extremely wrong about that, and this ownership has been wrong about damn near every draft pick it has made over the last eight-plus years. 2018: The Warriors draft Jacob Evans, whose NBA career lasts less than two full seasons, five picks before Jalen Brunson. 2020: The Warriors have the No. 2 overall pick and can therefore draft anyone not named Anthony Edwards. That list includes, among many others, LaMelo Ball, Tyrese Haliburton, Tyrese Maxey, Devin Vassell and Deni Avdija. But Lacob watches a James Wiseman workout and thinks he's found the next David Robinson. 2021: The Warriors don't just take Jonathan Kuminga over Trey Murphy III (who much of the front office favored), they take him over Franz Wagner. And then, with a chance at a re-do seven picks later, they take Moses Moody at No. 14 when Murphy III was still on the board, as were Alperen Sengun and Jalen Johnson, both of whom have become All-Stars. The 2020 and 2021 drafts, in particular, were supposed to set up Golden State's future, and they became the basis for the ill-fated two-timeline plan. The organization was too slow, or stubborn, or probably both, to ditch that plan and trade some of those guys while they still had some value. 
Wiseman and Kuminga basically were given away. Moody has been a fine rotation guy, ho-hum by lottery pick standards, while Brandin Podziemski, taken with the 19th pick in 2023, has been solid (don't listen to the idiots who say Podz has been a disaster; it's not even close to true). But those players are not home runs. Even at 23 years old, Yaxel looks like a home run. And beyond what this means for Golden State's long-term outlook, it begs the question of whether he changes the short-term plans for a front office that had seemingly conceded to a lost season as it gears up for a 2027 cap-space splurge. Is Lendeborg really good enough already to make the Warriors think they are a piece away from contention? Bill Simmons seemed to suggest as much when he recently declared that "Yaxel might have single-handedly saved the Steph era" while comparing him to 2010s LeBron James. 
If you audibly laughed at a prime-LeBron comp, you're not alone. But it speaks to the kind of buzz Lendeborg is generating, and the Warriors are definitely feeling it, too. Might they look at trading, say, Draymond Green, who's on an expiring contract? Perhaps they could pair Green with Kristaps Porzingis, who's only guaranteed $3 million next season, for close to $50 million in trade value. Add some draft equity to that package, and you can go hunting for some pretty big game. What about Trey Murphy III. What about adding Moody in and going after Anthony Davis? Imagine a Warriors team with Curry, who's still playing at an All-NBA level, Yaxel and a third All-Star to be named, with Jimmy Butler still coming back. Or you could trade Butler with some draft picks and do any of the same things. Before Yaxel shot out of a cannon, the Warriors seemed way too far away from even fringe contention to justify an all-in trade. You can argue they've been too focused on the blockbuster trades at the expense of the more peripheral moves that could've kept Curry competitive, like the ones the Knicks made for OG Anunoby (who, incidentally, was another Warriors "target") and Mikal Bridges, and Yaxel, in his career infancy, feels like that caliber of player. Not a star (yet), but a guy who can provide contention-level star support. Maybe the Steph Curry doesn't have to die on the vine after all. 
Bear in mind, the Warriors would have to trade draft picks to make anything happen, and for all the fans who love to mortgage the future, remember, this summer there were a lot of people who wanted the Warriors to trade the No. 11 pick with which they drafted Yaxel. So be careful what you wish for. That said, they got Yaxel. The Warriors have been wrong about a lot in post-Kevin Durant era, but all signs point toward them being absolutely right about Lendeborg. And now that they have him, it's fair to wonder if he covers enough of their future to actually start trying to maximize their present.

Arizona has won five straight games, including three straight in Big 12 play by an average of 28.0 points per game. In their only meeting as Big 12 opponents, the Red Raiders outlasted the Wildcats 28-22 as Fifita threw for 300 yards, but served up two interceptions.   Texas Tech vs. Arizona: Need to know  Inconsistent play: Despite the 6-1 start, Texas Tech has struggled to find consistency on either side of the ball. The Red Raiders rank in the bottom half of both total offense and defense in the Big 12 as neither unit has strung together consistent performances. For comparison, Texas Tech ranked top two in the Big 12 in both categories last season. Fifita's growth: The Arizona quarterback is setting career highs in every category during a sensational senior season for the Wildcats. Fifita leads the Big 12 with a 74% completion rate and a 174 passer rating, and ranks top 10 nationally in passing at just a shade under 295 yards per game. Since losing to BYU, Fifita has thrown for 275 yards and two touchdowns in every game during the five-game winning streak.

With the Derby della Madonnina set to take place later on Saturday, a victory for Roma would provide a significant boost and allow them to close the gap at the top of the table. The fixture also reminds AS Roma fans of a goal that made history, arguably one of the best scored by the legendary captain Francesco Totti in the Giallorossi jersey. You can watch Saturday's match between Udinese and AS Roma on CBS, and for all the best Serie A action all season long make sure to check out Paramount+.Totti, one of the most recognizable Italian football players in the history of the game, retired in 2017 and left an unforgettable mark at the club, winning the 2000-01 Serie A title, the last one won by the Giallorossi. Totti, who spent his whole career with his childhood club, scored 307 goals in 786 appearances for AS Roma. Some of those are still in the minds of AS Roma fans, such as the one scored against Udinese at the Stadio Olimpico in October 2002. How to watch Udinese vs. RomaDate: Saturday, Oct. 31 | Time: 1 p.m. ETLocation: Bluenergy Stadium -- Udine, ItalyTV: CBSOdds: Udinese +448; Draw +337; AS Roma -198Speaking to Corriere dello Sport on the goal scored at the Stadio Olimpico on October 2, 2002, Totti said: "For me, one of the best goals, aside from the ones I scored in Genoa, Inter and the derby, was a goal I scored against Udinese at the Stadio Olimpico. I scored twice that day... Batistuta dinks the ball over the goalkeeper, a little chip. I bring the ball under control with my head, I can't remember whether Bertotto was marking me and, with my back to goal, where De Sanctis was, I hit a volley on the half-bounce into the top corner at the far post."

Makhachev doesn't see himself hanging around long after unifying welterweight titles with Carlos Prates or Michael Morales

        Islam Makhachev doesn't see himself competing in mixed martial arts much longer. The reigning UFC welterweight champion is seeking the toughest challenge for what will be one of his final Octagon appearances.Makhachev once again turned his attention to Carlos Prates and Michael Morales on Friday. The top contenders will fight for the interim welterweight championship at UFC 336, scheduled to take place in Toronto on Jan. 30. Makhachev, already a two-division UFC champion with a record number of lightweight title defenses, wants to add at least one more elite welterweight to his resume before calling it a career. "My next fight is one of the last in my career," Makhachev wrote on social media. "They say Prates is too dangerous for me and Morales is too good for me.   So I want to face the best of them and prove to the world once again who is the best in the world."Makhachev has been unusually active on social media since the promotion booked the interim title fight. UFC CEO and president Dana White said the company planned for Makhachev to defend his title at UFC 336, but pivoted to the interim title fight because Makhachev woanted to wait until after Ramadan.
The fanbase is incredibly enthusiastic about Prates vs. Morales, but confused about why an interim title was introduced. In most cases, an interim title is created when the champion is unavailable for one year or indefinitely. Makhachev fought in August and could feasibly fight again in the spring. By comparison, UFC light heavyweight champion Carlos Ulberg tore his ACL in April, yet the promotion hasn't booked an interim title fight in that division. 
Makhachev is competing a little longer than his mentor, Khabib Nurmagomedov, wanted. Nurmagomedov publicly warned fighters about hanging onto glory once they reach 35. His pupil is no exception. Makhachev celebrated his 35th birthday in late October, but will likely be closer to 36 when he next competes.
